verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 9-10 roof photos show a sloped roof covered in brown/tan architectural asphalt shingles laid in overlapping courses, with ridge caps and a white valley/gutter channel. Exterior photo (p7) shows low-pitched overhanging roofs.
verdicts.rationale: Sloped tile-type covering clearly visible; it is asphalt shingle rather than clay/concrete tile, which is the closest form category ('Tiled'). Reviewer may want to confirm the L-foot/flashing detail suits shingles over RCC.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstructions on the roof that could affect the solar installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: Layout (p6-7) and roof photo (p9) show an existing PV array and an existing solar water heater (white tank visible on p9) on the roof; the two new south-roof module groups flank the water heater. Trees and a neighbouring multi-storey building visible beyond the eave (p9).
verdicts.rationale: Layout routes around existing equipment, but the water-heater tank sits directly between the two south-roof module groups and could cast morning/evening side shadow; not a clear contradiction, needs reviewer judgement.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Exterior photo (p7) shows low-pitched hip roofs; SketchUp layout (p6) annotated 'SLOPE: 15 Degrees'. Existing modules on p9 are flush-mounted parallel to the shingles.
verdicts.rationale: Flush-mount on a low-pitch roof means panel angle = roof slope; visual pitch is consistent with ~12-18°.

verdicts.question: In case of sloped roof, what is the slope angle of the roof? (in degrees)
verdicts.photo_observation: Exterior photo (p7) shows shallow hip roofs with wide overhangs; layout (p6) labelled 'SLOPE: 15 Degrees'.
verdicts.rationale: Visual roof pitch looks roughly 12-18°, consistent with 15°.

verdicts.question: On how many roofs at the site are we installing solar?
verdicts.photo_observation: Top view (p6) shows new modules on two hip-roof planes: 3 modules on the north plane and two groups of 2 (=4) on the south plane. Roof photo p9 annotated 'Roof 1 (South facing): 4 PV modules' and 'Roof 2 (North facing): 3 PV modules'.
verdicts.rationale: Two roof planes confirmed; 4+3 = 7 matches the 7-panel system. Note: p6 callout text reads 'South Roof: New PV-Modules (615Wp, 7 Nos.)' which conflicts with the drawn 4 modules - label typo to correct in the layout.
